sights.w: A nature theme park in Uruma's Ishikawa hills: water-buffalo cart rides, lake boat rides through subtropical forest and orchid viewing; you can also try on Ryukyu-era costume. Stars and Stripes Okinawa has covered it repeatedly as a family day out.

sights.n: National Theatre Okinawa (国立劇場おきなわ)
sights.w: Opened 18 January 2004 as Japan's fifth national theatre, built to preserve and present Okinawan traditional performing arts — above all kumiodori, the Ryukyuan court music-drama. A 632-seat main hall and a 255-seat small hall.

A gusuku built around 1453 by a local lord (aji) of Agena and a nationally designated Historic Site. Its concentric double ring of stone walls is described by Uruma City as the only surviving example of the type in Okinawa.

sights.n: Nakabaru Ruins, Ikei Island (仲原遺跡)
sights.address: Ikei, Uruma, Okinawa (centre of Ikei Island)
sights.w: A late-Jōmon-period village site near the middle of Ikei Island and a nationally designated Historic Site, with reconstructed pit dwellings. One of Uruma's four national historic sites.

sights.n: Shirumichu sacred cave, Hamahiga Island (シルミチュー霊場)
sights.w: A limestone cave up a 108-step stair behind a torii on Hamahiga Island, held to be where the Ryūkyū creator deities Shinerikyo and Amamikyo lived and raised their children — a place of prayer for fertility and harvest. The cave itself is normally closed and opened for Lunar New Year rites.
sights.k: Cave home of the creator gods
